newsitem.title: INDIA: Toyota India plant construction in Q1 1998.
newsitem.headline: Toyota India plant construction in Q1 1998.

text.p: Construction of Toyota Motor Corp's majority-owned Indian plant will start in the first quarter of 1998, a senior official of the firm's Indian partner, the Kirloskar group, said on Monday.

"We will apply to the Indian government for approval in about two months, and the construction of the plant will start by the first quarter of next year," Kiran Kulkarni, a senior executive at Mysore Kirloskar Ltd, told Reuters by telephone from the southern Indian city of Bangalore.

Earlier on Monday, Toyota, Japan's largest car maker, announced in Tokyo it will hold 74 percent equity in a $170 million joint venture with the Kirloskar group. It said it would make 50,000 multi-purpose vehicles, starting at the end of 1999, at a plant located in Bidadi, near Bangalore.
Kulkarni said several Kirloskar group firms will invest in 26 percent equity of the new company, which will be called Toyota Kirloskar Motors Ltd.
"We still have to decide on what the exact structure of the Kirloskar holding will be and which companies will invest in Toyota Kirloskar," Kulkarni said.

The Kirloskar group is a leading engineering group whose products include diesel engines, compressors, pumps, motors and castings. It has 10 listed companies, including the flagship Kirloskar Brothers Ltd.

Analysts expect India's market for cars to grow by around one million units in 2000/2001 (April-March) from 345,555 in 1995/96. The multi-purpose vehicle segment is estimated to grow to 250,000 units in calendar 2000 from 135,000 in calender 1996.
